segments.period: Fiscal year to 26 Sep 2026 vs 27 Sep 2025

why.Mac: Hardware in a mature PC market: part of the ecosystem but not its lock-in.
why.iPad: Flat sales in a mature tablet market.
why.Wearables, Home and Accessories: Flat sales; more competition than iPhone.

engines.source: Fiscal 2026 (10-K figures in the Q4 release): gross margin Products 39.3%, Services 76.2%; operating expenses 15.8% of revenue allocated by revenue, so operating margin ~23.5% Products, ~60.4% Services. Apple doesn't report profit by product, so all four product lines share the Products margin.

AAPL.moat_reason: ROIC 74% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 91%), at least 10 points above the 9.0% required return.
AAPL.r_reason: Mega-cap, very stable cash flows, huge buybacks: close to an average-risk stock.
AAPL.name: Apple Inc.
AAPL.notes: TTM to Sep-2026 (= fiscal 2026, year to 26 Sep 2026). Revenue $478.8B, +15.1% (iPhone +21% to $254.1B, Services +13% to $123.3B, Mac +13%, iPad and Wearables flat; Greater China +28%); September quarter +11.7% with iPhone +17% and Services +10%. Guidance for the December quarter: revenue +7-10%, Services +8-9%, gross margin 45-46% (down, mostly higher memory costs, which also limit Mac/iPad supply). FCF = OCF $145.1B - capex $9.0B = $136.1B; SBC $13.8B. FCF margin is flattered by low cash taxes; normalised SBC-adjusted margin 24.5% base (actual TTM 25.5%). Net cash $56.8B = cash $36.3B + marketable securities $100.6B (incl. $80.2B non-current) - commercial paper $2.0B - term debt $78.1B (leases excluded). Shares = Q4 diluted 14.63B; $86.4B bought back in FY26. Tax rate 17.0%. Risks: memory-cost squeeze on margins, App Store fee rulings (EU DMA, US Epic case), China and tariffs.

segments.period: Quarter to 30 Sep 2026 (FY27 Q1), year-ago recast from the stated growth (25%, -3%)

why.Devices and Consumer: Windows OEM, Xbox and Surface: mature, cyclical PC and console markets, sales shrinking 3%.

engines.source: Microsoft doesn't report operating income by its new segments, so both engines keep the company margin (margin_x 1).

MSFT.moat_reason: ROIC 30% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 34%), at least 10 points above the 9.0% required return.
MSFT.r_reason: Diversified software and cloud with recurring revenue and a net cash balance sheet.
MSFT.name: Microsoft Corp.
MSFT.notes: TTM to Sep-2026 (FY27 Q1). Revenue +19% in the quarter (Azure +48%). Cash capex $136B TTM ($39B in the quarter, double a year ago) crushes current FCF (OCF minus cash capex; finance-lease principal not deducted, as before); margin recovers as the build-out matures. Data-centre useful life extended to 25 years, so more new capacity comes via operating leases. Net cash = cash + investments minus bonds and non-current operating leases ($7B, down from $20B). FIN debt incl. leases is an ESTIMATE.

segments.period: Quarter to 30 Sep 2026 vs 30 Sep 2025 (hedging gains excluded)

why.Google Cloud: Third in cloud behind AWS and Azure; returns only recently above the hurdle.
why.Other Bets: Early-stage bets that lose money; no lasting edge yet.

engines.source: Measured Q3 2026 operating margins are Google Services 40.7%, Google Cloud 36.2%, Other Bets -550%, but Cloud carries most of the AI capex, so operating margin overstates its share of cash. Until segment capex is known, all engines keep the company cash margin (margin_x 1).

GOOGL.moat_reason: ROIC 31% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 36%), at least 10 points above the 10.0% required return.
GOOGL.r_reason: Strong balance sheet, but search faces AI disruption and regulatory risk.
GOOGL.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
GOOGL.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. Revenue +25% in Q3 (Cloud +103% to $30.7B). FCF = OCF - capex (company definition); TTM FCF fell to $19.7B as capex hit $51.4B in Q3 (FY26 capex guide $195-205B, 2027 reportedly >$300B), so the starting margin is very low and the value leans on the margin recovering. SBC $30.4B (actual; was estimated at $24.5B). 2026 financing: $42.9B new stock, $19.1B mandatory convertible preferred, $85B new debt. Net cash = cash + marketable securities - long-term debt. 'extra' = $135.2B non-marketable securities at a 50% haircut. Interest is the Q3 run-rate.

why.AWS: Top-two cloud platform with a 38% operating margin: a longer edge than retail.

engines.source: Measured trailing 12-month operating margins are North America 8.2%, International 3.3%, AWS 37.8%, but AWS also carries most of the capex, so operating margin overstates its share of cash (using it would lift fair value about 47%). Until segment capex is known, all engines keep the company cash margin (margin_x 1).

AMZN.moat_reason: Median ROIC 13% over 4 years, within 3 points of the 10.5% required return (goodwill from acquisitions can depress this).
AMZN.r_reason: Thin retail margins and very heavy AI capex make free cash flow volatile.
AMZN.name: Amazon.com Inc.
AMZN.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. FCF (Amazon's own definition: operating cash flow minus net capex) is -$42B on $211B net capex; margin recovers as the AI build-out matures. Q3 revenue +12%, Q4 guide +12-16%. SBC actual ($19.9B; was estimated at $22B). Net debt $158B incl. $99B long-term leases after ~$44B of new bonds in Q3. Interest is the Q3 run-rate; current debt portions estimated. Anthropic stake NOT valued (upside not counted).

NVDA.moat_reason: ROIC 27% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 104%), at least 10 points above the 10.0% required return.
NVDA.r_reason: Below the 11.5% chip-group rate: mega-cap, net cash and a dominant position. Still above average for cyclical AI spending, customer concentration and competition. 11-12% is also defensible.
NVDA.name: NVIDIA Corp.
NVDA.notes: TTM to Jul-2026 (FY27 Q2). SBC is an ESTIMATE (about 2.3% of revenue). Data-centre demand is highly cyclical and concentrated: lower confidence. Base case is deliberately below consensus growth. Base case is deliberately below consensus growth.

AVGO.moat_reason: Median ROIC 23% over 4 years, above the 10.0% required return but not consistently by 10+ points.
AVGO.r_reason: Chips plus a large recurring software business (VMware) lower the risk vs the chip group, offset by $35B net debt.
AVGO.name: Broadcom Inc.
AVGO.notes: TTM to Aug-2026 (FY26 Q3). SBC is an ESTIMATE (about 10% of revenue). Net debt from acquisitions. AI custom-chip demand drives growth.

LLY.moat_reason: ROIC 25% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 31%), at least 10 points above the 9.0% required return.
LLY.r_reason: Large diversified pharma; obesity-drug growth is strong but competition and pricing pressure are rising.
LLY.name: Eli Lilly and Co.
LLY.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. Q3 revenue +39% on Mounjaro/Zepbound; FY26 revenue guide $85-87B (as of Q2). SBC from filings (~$0.7B; the earlier $2.2B was an estimate). FCF = operating cash flow minus $11.0B PP&E capex on new plants; margin rises as the build-out matures. FCF excludes ~$18B of 2026 cash spent on acquired IPR&D and acquisitions. Interest expense is an ESTIMATE. Growth rests on obesity drugs; pricing and patent risk.

ADBE.moat_reason: ROIC 38% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 46%), at least 10 points above the 9.5% required return.
ADBE.r_reason: Recurring subscription revenue, but generative AI threatens its creative-software moat.
ADBE.name: Adobe Inc.
ADBE.notes: TTM to Aug-2026 (FY26 Q3). SBC is an ESTIMATE (about 8% of revenue). The bear case assumes generative-AI tools erode its creative-software moat (sales shrink first, then recover slowly); the market price looks close to that view.

APP.moat_reason: Median ROIC 33% over 4 years, above the 11.0% required return but not consistently by 10+ points.
APP.r_reason: Very high margins that depend on one ad platform, short track record, regulatory and accounting scrutiny.
APP.name: AppLovin Corp.
APP.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. Revenue $7.61B TTM (FY25 $5.48B + 9M-26 $5.95B - 9M-25 $3.82B), all advertising since the Apps business was sold in mid-2025. Q3 revenue +55% to $2.18B, adjusted EBITDA margin 84%, net income +72%. Q4 guide: revenue $2.365-2.395B (+43-44%), adjusted EBITDA margin 84-85%. The Q4 run-rate alone is ~25% above TTM revenue, so base year-1 growth raised from 25% to 30% (bear 10% -> 15%, bull 40% -> 45%); margins kept. FCF = operating cash flow - capex - finance-lease principal (company definition) $4.88B TTM (sum of Q4'25-Q3'26 releases), 64% of revenue. Stock pay $0.33B TTM (actual, from the adjusted EBITDA reconciliations; replaces the earlier estimate). Net debt $0.34B = $3.17B cash - $3.52B notes. Diluted shares 334.8M (Q3 average), down ~2% a year from buybacks ($1.4B in Q3, authorisation raised to $3.6B). Very high margins, reliance on one ad engine (AXON), platform rules at Apple and Google, short-seller and regulatory scrutiny, and heavy reliance on terminal value: lower confidence. Higher required return (11%) and 35% safety margin.

FICO.moat_reason: ROIC 44% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 49%), at least 10 points above the 9.5% required return.
FICO.r_reason: Near-monopoly in credit scores, but pricing power is under regulatory pressure and it carries net debt.
FICO.name: Fair Isaac Corp.
FICO.notes: TTM to Sep-2026 (fiscal year FY26 = TTM). Revenue $2.53B, up 27% (scores $1.65B, up 41%, from a higher mortgage-originations score price despite high-single-digit lower mortgage volumes; software up, ARR +14% with platform ARR +72%, net retention 112%). Q4 revenue +27%. FCF = operating cash flow $1.07B minus capex $0.04B (incl. capitalised software) = $1.03B; actual stock pay $0.19B (was an 8%-of-revenue estimate), so FCF after stock pay is 33% of revenue, about 40% before interest. Net debt $5.0B = cash and marketable securities $0.27B less $5.26B of debt (term loan, revolver, senior notes; FY26 buybacks of $3.0B, ~10% of shares, were debt-funded) and $0.02B of leases; net interest $0.22B; tax rate 24% (less excess tax benefit from stock pay). Buybacks paused in Q4 to repay the term loan. NO FY27 GUIDANCE: management withdrew it while it moves to custom (bespoke) mortgage pricing; the FICO Preferred Program freezes the 2027 wholesale score price for enrolled lenders. Scenarios CUT after the Oct-2026 price-drop review (lasting cause) and kept: the FHFA lets all lenders deliver VantageScore to Fannie/Freddie (Sep 2026), FHA accepts it from Jan 2027, Rocket made VantageScore its preferred score and FICO froze its mortgage score price, ending the price rises behind its margin gains (mortgage ~60% of scores revenue). Management says no meaningful volume lost to competition yet, but the price effect shows only in calendar 2027. Base growth 7% (consensus was ~8% before the guidance was withdrawn) with the cash margin held at ~38% instead of expanding; bear: mortgage share loss and price cuts, ~1% growth and a 30% margin; bull 11% / 42%.

APA.moat_reason: Base growth -4.0% now, 2.0% in year 10: at or below 2.5%, so no advantage period is added (margins carry the decline, as before).
APA.r_reason: Above the 8.5% Energy rate: an oil producer with Egypt and exploration risk, net debt and oil-price dependence.
APA.name: APA Corporation
APA.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. Revenue $9.46B (statement total revenues: 9M26 $7,469M + FY25 $8,920M - 9M25 $6,929M), earned at an average realised oil price of about $82.5/bbl over the four quarters ($61 / $79 / $98 / $92); the September quarter was up 31% on a year earlier purely on price (oil $92.02 vs $67.43) while production fell 3% (450k BOE/d). Brent is still ~$93 on Middle East / Strait of Hormuz risk and fell ~5% on 9 Nov on hopes of an Iran deal, so prices remain near a cycle high: every case still assumes revenue falls and the cash margin shrinks from today's ~21% (after SBC) toward 10-20%. FCF $2.1B = operating cash flow $4.44B - additions to oil and gas property $2.34B (TTM); company raised its own 2026 FCF outlook to ~$2.9B and set a preliminary 2027 capital budget of $2.5B (2026 ~$2.1B). SBC kept at ~$0.15B/yr: expensed stock- and cash-settled pay was $0.19B TTM, but the jump is cash-settled awards marked up with the share price, which are already in operating cash flow. Net debt $3.2B (debt $3.30B + finance leases $0.03B - cash $0.08B), after $450M of buybacks in the quarter (shares 336M at 31 Oct). Egypt oil output keeps slipping (116k b/d gross). Oil-price dependent: lower confidence, 10% required return and 35% safety margin.

DECK.moat_reason: ROIC 49% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 92%), at least 10 points above the 9.5% required return.
DECK.r_reason: Fashion and brand risk (HOKA, UGG) and tariffs, partly offset by $1.1B net cash.
DECK.name: Deckers Outdoor Corp.
DECK.notes: TTM to Sep-2026 (FY27 Q2). Growth slowing: Q2 sales +3.5% (HOKA +6.8%, UGG +3.5%). FY27 guidance CUT to revenue $5.700-5.725B (+4-5%; was $5.86-5.91B), HOKA high-single-digit, UGG low-single-digit, operating margin ~23% incl. ~150bp IEEPA tariff refunds, EPS $7.80-7.95. Base growth cut to 5% and bull to 8% (from 6% / 10%) after the guidance cut. SBC now from filings (~$46M). TTM FCF $1.05B includes ~$46M one-off tariff refunds (~$1.02B without). Net cash $0.67B (cash $1.21B less $0.54B leases) at the seasonal low after $638M of buybacks in H1. Fashion/brand risk: the bear case assumes HOKA growth stalls.

INCY.moat_reason: Median ROIC 31% over 4 years, above the 9.5% required return but not consistently by 10+ points.
INCY.r_reason: Jakafi is ~60% of sales and loses patent protection later this decade.
INCY.name: Incyte Corp.
INCY.notes: TTM to Sep-2026, revenue cut by the one-off $246M Opzelura settlement benefit (Q2-26). FCF NORMALISED to $1.95B: the one-off $1.27B Vega (latarcibart) upfront, paid in Q3-2026 through operating cash flow and expensed as IPR&D, is excluded (reported TTM FCF $0.69B). Net cash $3.85B cash and securities less finance leases; Vega already paid. 2026 net sales guidance raised to $5.21-5.30B (Opzelura +36%, other Heme/Onc +42% in Q3, Jakafi +4%). SBC ~$0.26B/yr. Diluted shares estimated (~206M). Jakafi is ~60% of sales and faces loss of exclusivity later this decade, so the bear case has shrinking sales and lower margins; 35% safety margin.

MKC.moat_reason: Median ROIC 9% over 4 years, within 3 points of the 8.0% required return (goodwill from acquisitions can depress this).
MKC.r_reason: Below the 9% Consumer Defensive rate: spices are very stable demand. Note the pending Unilever Foods deal adds leverage risk.
MKC.name: McCormick & Co.
MKC.notes: TTM to Aug-2026. Trailing P/E is distorted by a one-off $867M gain on taking control of McCormick de Mexico (Jan-2026), so this model uses free cash flow. Organic growth ~3-6%. STANDALONE value only: the pending Unilever Foods combination (McCormick holders to own 35%, $15.7B cash to Unilever, close expected mid-2027) would change the per-share value substantially. Lower confidence.

EXPE.moat_reason: Median ROIC 32% over 4 years, above the 10.5% required return but not consistently by 10+ points.
EXPE.r_reason: Online travel agent: cyclical, and the most exposed to AI agents booking directly with hotels and airlines.
EXPE.name: Expedia Group Inc.
EXPE.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. Revenue $16.2B (+12% in the September quarter to $4.94B); gross bookings +11% to $34.0B, room nights +7%, B2B bookings +19% vs B2C +7%. Full-year 2026 guidance raised to revenue $16.37-16.43B (+11-12%) and bookings +10%, but the December quarter is guided to only +4-6% revenue and +3-5% bookings. FCF NORMALISED at $3.72B (the same ~23% margin as before): reported TTM FCF is $3.75B (9M26 $3,627M + FY25 $3,110M - 9M25 $2,991M), so at September, after the seasonal outflow of customer prepayments, the normalised and reported figures agree; at mid-year the TTM figure is swollen by merchant bookings. Cash ($5.0B + $0.5B short-term investments) is mostly customers' money (deferred merchant bookings $12.6B), so net cash is set to zero (net debt $0.1B incl. $0.2B leases offset). Shares 121M (118.6M class A + B outstanding plus ~2.4M dilution); buybacks $1.7B in 9M26. SBC $0.44B TTM. Main risk: AI agents (e.g. Meta's Muse) booking directly with hotels and airlines and bypassing aggregators; the bear case has flat sales and margins squeezed to 12%. 35% safety margin.

BKNG.moat_reason: ROIC 116% or more in each of the last 1 years (median 116%), at least 10 points above the 9.5% required return.
BKNG.r_reason: Dominant online travel platform with strong direct traffic; travel is cyclical and AI agents are a new disintermediation risk.
BKNG.name: Booking Holdings Inc.
BKNG.notes: TTM to Sep-2026 (prices and shares after the April 2026 25-for-1 split). Reported Q3 revenue fell 1% only because of a one-off FTC charge (Priceline / Guest Reservations case): a $900M revenue reduction plus a $100M accrued loss, not yet settled. Revenue here is adjusted ($29.0B TTM, Q3 adjusted +8.7%); the expected ~$1.0B payment is taken off the value via 'extra' (-$1.0B; the FTC may seek more). Q3: room nights +6.7%, gross bookings +9.6% (+11% cc). Guidance: Q4 slows sharply (room nights +1-3%, adjusted revenue +0-2%, +2-4% cc, EBITDA about flat) on softer international travel and the Middle East; FY26 high single digits; margin-expansion goal dropped. Base year-1 growth cut from 8% to 7% for the Q4 slowdown. FCF = OCF $9.56B - capex $0.32B = $9.24B, SBC $0.59B; SBC-adjusted cash margin ~30% of adjusted revenue. Net debt $5.0B = cash $15.8B - debt $20.1B - leases ~$0.7B. Shares = Q3 diluted 753M ($9.9B bought back in 9M). Main risk: AI agents bypassing online travel agencies; Booking's direct traffic and hotel supply make it less exposed than Expedia, so the bear case still grows slowly with margins down to 26%. Also regulators (FTC, EU DMA).

INTU.moat_reason: Median ROIC 17% over 4 years, above the 10.0% required return but not consistently by 10+ points.
INTU.r_reason: Sticky TurboTax / QuickBooks franchises, but AI tax and bookkeeping agents are a real threat to pricing power.
INTU.name: Intuit Inc.
INTU.notes: FY to Jul-2026. FCF NORMALISED to $7.3B: FY26 reported $8.6B vs $6.1B in FY25 (timing). Stock pay is large (~10% of revenue), so the SBC-adjusted margin is ~24%. FY27 guidance: revenue +9-10% ($23.3-23.5B), GAAP EPS $20.12-20.36. Shares are down sharply in 2026 on fears that AI tax and bookkeeping agents erode TurboTax and QuickBooks; the bear case halves growth and trims margins.

ADSK.moat_reason: ROIC 33% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 40%), at least 10 points above the 10.0% required return.
ADSK.r_reason: Design software with high switching costs; exposed to construction and manufacturing cycles and AI-native design tools.
ADSK.name: Autodesk Inc.
ADSK.notes: TTM to Jul-2026. Revenue growing ~15% (helped by the shift to annual billing and the new transaction model); analysts expect ~11% next year. SBC is heavy (~9% of revenue). FY26 SBC-adjusted margin was 22%, TTM 27%; base target 27%. Small net cash. Risk: AI-native design tools and a construction slowdown.

TPR.moat_reason: Median ROIC 25% over 4 years, above the 10.0% required return but not consistently by 10+ points.
TPR.r_reason: Fashion brand (Coach) risk and tariffs; store leases add leverage.
TPR.name: Tapestry Inc.
TPR.notes: TTM to Sep-2026 (fiscal Q1 FY27, quarter to 26 Sep 2026). Coach brand still strong: Q1 Coach sales +16% (constant currency), Kate Spade -10%, total sales +11% to $1.89B; GAAP gross margin 78.6% (+230 bp), operating margin 22.4%. FY27 outlook raised: sales $8.5-8.6B (+6-7% constant currency), EPS $8.25-8.35, adjusted FCF approaching $1.7B, $1.7B of buybacks; Q2 guided +5-6%, so the base case's 5% growth stands. FCF = operating cash flow - capex (statement) $1.88B TTM, stock pay $0.11B; SBC-adjusted cash margin ~21.6% (history ~15%), so the base target is 17%, not today's peak. Inventory +4% vs sales +11%. Net debt $3.4B = $0.78B cash and short-term investments - $2.56B borrowings - $1.67B store lease liabilities. Diluted shares 204.5M (Q1 average; ~200M guided for FY27 after buybacks). Fashion and tariff risk, Kate Spade still shrinking, one-brand reliance: the bear case has sales falling and margins back to 13%. 35% safety margin.

VEEV.moat_reason: ROIC 57% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 68%), at least 10 points above the 9.5% required return.
VEEV.r_reason: Mission-critical life-sciences software with large net cash; risk from Salesforce competition in CRM.
VEEV.name: Veeva Systems Inc.
VEEV.notes: TTM to Jul-2026. Life-sciences cloud software; $7.1B net cash (~14% of market value). Stock pay ~14% of revenue, so the SBC-adjusted margin is ~34%. Analysts expect ~12% growth. Risks: customers moving CRM back to Salesforce and pharma budget cuts; bear case 7% growth.

MNST.moat_reason: ROIC 28% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 31%), at least 10 points above the 8.5% required return.
MNST.r_reason: Below the 9% Consumer Defensive rate: very stable demand, no debt, long growth record.
MNST.name: Monster Beverage Corp.
MNST.notes: TTM to Sep-2026 (prices after the 2-for-1 stock split). Energy drinks; Q3 net sales +16.7% to a record $2.56B (+16.3% currency-adjusted), 9M +20.9%; international now ~47% of sales (+28.1%, LATAM +48.8%). Gross margin slipped to 54.7% (55.7%) on higher aluminium can costs, mix and freight, partly offset by price increases. No formal guidance; analysts expect ~10% next year. FCF = operating cash flow minus capex ($1.92B TTM, down from $2.08B because receivables rose $362M and inventories $127M with the fast growth). SBC-adjusted cash margin ~19% (base target 21% as working capital normalises). No debt; net cash $3.6B = cash $2.15B + short-term investments $1.56B less ~$0.09B leases ($0.93B long-term investments not counted). Risk: competition (Celsius, Red Bull), aluminium/tariff costs; bear case 4% growth.

ALLE.moat_reason: Median ROIC 21% over 4 years, above the 9.0% required return but not consistently by 10+ points.
ALLE.r_reason: Steady locks and access-control business; tied to the non-residential construction cycle, moderate debt.
ALLE.name: Allegion plc
ALLE.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. Locks and access control; Q3 revenue +9.6% (organic +7.2%). FY26 guidance raised: revenue +9.5-10.5% reported / +5-6% organic, adjusted EPS $9.05-9.10. TTM FCF $0.74B incl. ~$20M one-off IEEPA tariff refunds. SBC is an ESTIMATE (~$30M; FY25 $29.8M). Net debt $1.84B now includes $0.19B operating leases (was $1.71B excl. leases). Buybacks $280M YTD. Risk: non-residential construction cycle.

FTNT.moat_reason: ROIC not measurable from the statements (negative or tiny invested capital), so the middle class by default. Check by hand.
FTNT.r_reason: Cybersecurity is durable demand, but firewall hardware refresh cycles make growth lumpy.
FTNT.name: Fortinet Inc.
FTNT.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. FCF NORMALISED to $2.85B (~36% of revenue, same margin as before): reported TTM $3.43B is inflated by prepaid service contracts (billings +29% vs revenue +20% in Q3; deferred revenue $7.9B); FY25 was $2.2B. Firewall refresh lifted FY26 revenue growth to ~20% (guide $8.13-8.22B); analysts expect ~11% next year as it fades. $4.3B net cash (cash + ST investments - $0.5B notes). Risk: hardware cycle and competition (Palo Alto, cloud security).

RMD.moat_reason: Median ROIC 23% over 4 years, above the 9.0% required return but not consistently by 10+ points.
RMD.r_reason: Healthcare device leader with recurring masks revenue; GLP-1 drugs are a long-term demand risk.
RMD.name: ResMed Inc.
RMD.notes: TTM to Sep-2026 (FY27 Q1), PRO FORMA excluding MatrixCare (sold for $490M, closed in the quarter; ~$220M/yr revenue): revenue ~$5.53B, FCF ~$1.55B (reported TTM $5.73B / $1.59B; the split is estimated). Sleep-apnoea devices and masks; SBC-adjusted cash margin ~26%, small net cash after a $0.94B buyback in the quarter. FY27 guidance 5-7% core constant-currency growth ($5.75-5.85B reported). Interest is an estimate. Risk: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs shrinking the apnoea patient pool (so far demand has held up); bear case 2% growth.

V.moat_reason: ROIC 41% or more in each of the last 4 years (median 45%), at least 10 points above the 8.5% required return.
V.r_reason: Above the 7.5% financials rate: payment networks are very durable but face regulation and new payment rails.
V.name: Visa Inc.
V.notes: FY to Sep-2026 (fiscal Q4 reported 27 Oct 2026). Network with ~46% SBC-adjusted cash margin; FY26 net revenue +15% (Q4 +13%), FCF $22.1B. FY27 guidance: adjusted net revenue growth low double digits, adjusted EPS growth low double digits to low teens. Net debt $8.0B (excl. $0.6B litigation escrow). Shares now = diluted class-A as-converted (1.882B, includes class B/C); the previous 1.704B was class A only, which overstated value per share by ~10%. Risks: US interchange regulation (Credit Card Competition Act), real-time payments and stablecoins; bear case 7% growth and margin 41%.

FIX.moat_reason: Median ROIC 33% over 4 years, above the 11.0% required return but not consistently by 10+ points.
FIX.r_reason: Construction contractor at a cyclical peak driven by AI data-centre spending; earnings can fall fast if that slows.
FIX.name: Comfort Systems USA Inc.
FIX.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. Mechanical and electrical contractor riding the AI data-centre build-out: Q3 revenue +54%, backlog $17.8B (+90% YoY; $14.1B in June). ROE was about 40% TTM after large rate increases, a light catastrophe year and gains from selling the group and voluntary benefits businesses; it was negative in 2022-2023 when claim costs outran prices. 10-year median ROE ~12%. Analysts expect EPS to fall from $44 TTM to ~$28 next year (ROE ~23%), so the starting ROE is 21%, fading to 15% in the base case (11% bear, 18% bull). Book value grows with premiums: 4.5% fading to 3.5%. Common book value $30.3B ($2.0B preferred stock excluded). Risks: catastrophes (wildfires, hurricanes, convective storms), auto claim inflation, state rate regulators. Growth Screen insurance top-5 pick: 9% required return, 30% safety margin.

HIG.name: The Hartford Insurance Group Inc.

Analysts expect EPS of ~$13.60 next year (ROE ~20%), so the starting ROE is 18%, fading to 15% in the base case (11.5% bear, 17.5% bull). Book value grows 5% fading to 3.5%. Common book value $18.5B ($0.33B preferred excluded); diluted shares ~273.5M (ESTIMATE). Risks: softer commercial prices, reserve charges on older liability years, catastrophes. Growth Screen insurance top-5 pick: 8.5% required return, 25% safety margin.

AIZ.name: Assurant Inc.
AIZ.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. Two businesses: Global Lifestyle (phone and car protection plans and extended warranties sold through carriers, retailers and car dealers; mostly fee-like) and Global Housing (lender-placed and renters insurance, exposed to hurricanes). Valued as an insurer on book value and return on equity. ROE 14-16% in 2023-2025 and ~18% TTM (net income $1.07B; 18.2% annualised in the September quarter). September quarter: Global Lifestyle adjusted EBITDA +15% to $237M (Connected Living +23% on mobile trade-in and device protection; 7.6M mobile devices serviced vs 4.8M a year earlier), Global Housing adjusted EBITDA ex catastrophes +11% to $288M; catastrophes $20M. Nine-month adjusted EPS $18.47 (+30%). The company raised its 2026 outlook: adjusted EBITDA ex catastrophes up ~10% and adjusted EPS up low double digits; Global Lifestyle EBITDA up mid-to-high teens; buybacks $350M. The starting ROE is 18%, fading to 15.5% in the base case (12% bear, 18% bull): Global Lifestyle's fee-like protection plans earn more on their capital than the housing book. Book value grows 5% fading to 3.5%. Book value $6.0B (down slightly from June on unrealised investment losses in AOCI; $6.9B excluding AOCI) includes ~$3.1B of goodwill and intangibles from acquisitions. Diluted shares 49.7M (September-quarter weighted average). Risks: hurricanes in Global Housing, losing a large carrier or retail partner, lower phone upgrades. Growth Screen insurance top-5 pick: 9% required return, 30% safety margin.

NMIH.moat_reason: ROE 16-18% over 4 years (Yahoo statements; median 18%), more than 3 points above the 10% required return. Mortgage insurance is an oligopoly of six with capital rules that keep new entrants out. Underwriter: 15 years, then halfway to the required return.

NMIH.name: NMI Holdings Inc.
NMIH.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. US private mortgage insurance (National MI): it pays the lender part of the loss when a borrower with less than 20% down defaults. Valued as an insurer on book value and return on equity. ROE 16-18% in 2022-2025 and ~15% TTM (13.8% annualised in the September quarter: claims rose to $29.1M from $18.6M a year earlier and the default rate to 1.23% from 1.05%) as excess capital builds. Net income $393M TTM; insurance in force $229.7B, up 5%. Analysts expect EPS of ~$5.10-5.30 this year and ~$5.50 next (ROE ~14.5%), so the starting ROE is 14.5%, base 13.5% (9% bear: a housing downturn with falling prices raises claims; 15.5% bull). Book value grows 6% fading to 3% (insurance in force grows with mortgage lending). Book value $2.70B ($36.13 a share, up 11% in a year); PMIERs available assets $3.8B vs $2.2B required. No dividend, buys back ~2-3% of shares a year ($27M in the quarter). Diluted shares 76.1M (Q3 weighted average). Risks: house prices and unemployment (defaults are edging up), Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac capital rules (PMIERs) and their possible privatisation, price competition among the six US mortgage insurers. Russell 2000 small cap (passes all 5 checks under the Insurance filter): 10% required return, 35% safety margin.

Analysts expect EPS to fall from $8.0 TTM to ~$5.60 next year (ROE ~24%). Starting ROE 22%, base 14% over a full storm cycle (6% bear: a major Florida hurricane every few years; 18% bull). Risks: a major Florida hurricane, reinsurance costs (it buys reinsurance for most of a 1-in-100-year storm), Florida politics. PLMR.name: Palomar Holdings Inc.
PLMR.notes: TTM to Sep-2026. Specialty property insurance (earthquake, commercial and residential property, inland marine, builders' risk, crop, surety) and fronting, mostly in the US. Valued as an insurer on book value and return on equity. ROE rose from 14% in 2022 to 24% in 2025 (~23% TTM, net income $217M; 26.6% annualised in the September quarter, 33% on the company's adjusted basis that adds back stock pay, intangibles amortisation and deal costs). September quarter: gross written premiums +28% to $767M, net written premiums +41%, combined ratio 80.8% (78.1% a year earlier), catastrophe losses only $4.5M. The company raised 2026 guidance to adjusted net income of $280-285M (~$10.40-10.55 per share, incl. $8-12M of catastrophe losses). Starting ROE 24% (raised from 23% on the stronger run-rate), base 19% (14% bear, 23% bull). Book value grows 20% next year fading to 4% (bear 10%, bull 25%): fast growth needs capital, so little cash is paid out in the early years. Book value $0.985B incl. $0.23B goodwill and intangibles (Gray Surety, First Indemnity); tangible equity $0.76B. Now carries a term loan (interest $5M in the quarter). Diluted shares 27.0M (September-quarter weighted average). Risks: a large California earthquake (reinsured up to a 1-in-250-year event), reinsurance prices, competition in commercial earthquake, crop-loss swings. P/B is ~4.2, so the price needs high ROE for a long time. Russell 2000 small cap (passes all 5 checks under the Insurance filter): 10.5% required return, 35% safety margin.

ROE 19% in 2022, falling to 12% in 2025 and ~12% TTM (11.7% annualised in the September quarter) as capital built up faster than insurance in force. PMIERs sufficiency 177%. Diluted shares 89.8M (Q3 weighted average, down 9% in a year). Risks: house prices and unemployment (rising defaults), Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac capital rules and their possible privatisation, price competition. Russell 2000 small cap (passes 4 of 5 checks under the Insurance filter): 10% required return, 35% safety margin.

Russell 2000 small cap (passes 4 of 5 checks under the Insurance filter): 10% required return, 35% safety margin.
